correctness.rationale: For every prime power q≡7 (mod8), t²−6t+1=0 has two distinct nonzero non±1 roots (since 2 is a square, char odd). For monic X²+uX+v, z=(u²−4v)/4 converts simultaneous irreducibility at shifts {−t,−1,1,t} to four negative quadratic characters, with q coefficient choices per z. Expanding H(z)=Π(1−chi(z−s)) gives pair total −6 and cancellation of cubic sums under z↦−z. The projective Mobius identity [(A²−B²)(A²−t²B²)]=−(t+1)^4[(z²−1)(z²−t²)] defines a bijection of P¹, and chi(−1)=−1 forces the projective sum zero; removing infinity gives affine quartic character sum −1. Hence ΣH=q−7. The four exceptional z corrections B are 0 or 8 (at most one exceptional z can have all opposite differences nonsquare), and 16-divisibility fixes B by q mod16, so N=floor((q−7)/16), M=qN. Independently verified homogeneous polynomial identity modulo t²−6t+1 symbolically and counted 8 prime-field cases including q=7,23,31,47,71,79,103,127; these are corroborative, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: A canonical harmonic four-point configuration yields a uniform *exact* irreducibility count over infinitely many prime powers, including a sharp vanishing threshold and cancellation of the usual genus-one quartic fluctuation. This is a substantive exact-function-field prime-tuple invariant, not a finite table or only asymptotic specialization; limited to a special symmetric configuration.

limitations: Only q≡7 modulo 8 and the specific harmonic symmetric set; other four-tuples may retain an elliptic fluctuation.
Extension-field uniformity follows algebraically; independent finite checks were only prime fields, not an exhaustive examination of all prime powers.
